answer: An agent marketplace requires each trading identity to lock a fixed bond for 30 days before accepting jobs. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up 1,000 bonds, imposing a capital cost even if registration is free. The defense rests on locked funds, not an identity’s polished fable. Its limit is clear as crystal: wealthy attackers can still buy influence, but each extra vine on the marketplace’s trellis needs its own bond.
